title: SEO & AEO Auditing
intro: Search auditing has attracted a cluster of bots, and lately as much attention on how models describe a brand as on how search engines rank it. The mechanical parts of the job suit an agent well: crawling a site, finding broken things, checking whether pages say what they claim, tracking positions over time. Those are checkable tasks with unambiguous answers. The interpretive part suits it much less. A bot can tell you a page is thin; whether that matters depends on what the page is for, and most listings will happily generate a hundred recommendations without ranking them. Treat the output as a list of findings rather than a plan. The more interesting recent listings check what an assistant says when asked about your product, which is a genuinely new job rather than an old one automated.

bots.fitReason: Purpose-built site audit: SEO, content, speed, accessibility, CRO and schema, scored and bucketed P0/P1/P2 with evidence URLs and a monthly diff. It is a findings list rather than a prioritised plan, and it covers classic search rather than what assistants say about you.

Runs AI Overviews, Answer Engine and Generative Engine Optimization as a standing programme rather than a one-off prompt check, which is the newer half of this job. Weaker on the mechanical crawl-and-break-things side.

Covers SEO and AEO together, reads whatever you have already connected and only asks for the gaps. More of an ongoing programme teammate than a one-shot auditor, so expect setup questions before you get findings.

Watches rival sites, search rankings and AI-answer visibility over time, so it does the tracking-positions part properly. It is pointed at competitors rather than auditing your own site, so it is a complement to an audit, not one.

A general senior-marketer bot spanning SEO, GEO, Google Ads, Meta and Shopify, so search auditing is one of several things it will discuss. Thin description and no stated crawl or scoring method — do not expect a structured audit report.
